clue.text: Their offerings are bound to be available to members

definitions.text: Their offerings are bound to be available to members

parts.words: Their offerings are bound to be available to members
parts.note: the 'offerings' are books, 'bound' in covers rather than certain, and supplied to people who have signed up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' reads as 'certain to be', but here it means books in bindings sent out to subscribers.
explanation.definitionFit: Such societies send their subscribers a monthly selection of hardback volumes at a discount.

clue.text: Fish in British stream

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A fish is spotted swimming in a British brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is a European flatfish related to the turbot, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Fail to turn out as expected

definitions.text: Fail to turn out as expected

parts.words: Fail to turn out as expected
parts.note: 'turn out' here means get out of bed at the expected hour, not prove to be

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as something going wrong, but 'turn out' is getting up in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying asleep past the alarm means failing to rise at the planned time.

clue.text: Disciplining person having another drink, having imbibed quite a lot

indicators.note: a drink that has 'imbibed' something has taken it in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a chaser is a drink taken after another one
ten is a fair number, so 'quite a lot'

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps others in line takes one more drink after already downing plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: One who chastens is a person who corrects or punishes others to improve them.

clue.text: Leading ordinary lives, like some twins?

definitions.meaning: people of no special note live unremarkable lives
identical twins may be impossible to tell apart

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both commonplace and, read literally, not told apart from one another.

clue.text: Kind of dog experts criticize in plausible story line

indicators.note: the experts and the criticism are placed in the story line, inside it

parts.note: a spiel is glib persuasive patter
a ringer, in Australian usage, is the top shearer in a shed, hence an expert
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Experts find fault with the persuasive patter they are being fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringer' as an expert is Australian shearing slang for the fastest hand in the shed; 'plausible story line' is the sales patter that wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of gundog, used to flush game, in English and Welsh varieties.

clue.text: One's needed in fall for thrashing

definitions.text: One's needed in fall for thrashing

indicators.note: the one is required inside the word for a drop, so it goes in
the letters are beaten about and scattered, as grain is when it is threshed

parts.note: taken as written
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone must be in the autumn harvest to beat the grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed in' puts I inside FALL to make FAILL, and 'thrashing' then scrambles those letters. The whole clue describes the tool too.
explanation.definitionFit: A flail is a hand tool with a swinging bar, and the whole clue pictures it beating grain from the ears.

clue.text: Last female in a line

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The final woman standing in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Final and last are synonyms, both meaning coming at the end.

clue.text: Acknowledge nobody is debt-free after cut

indicators.note: a word that is cut loses its end, so the last letter of the phrase goes

parts.note: if nobody is free of debt, then everyone owes: all owe

explanation.surface: Admit that, following the cuts, everyone owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After cut' tells you to take the phrase ALL OWE and clip its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow a point is to concede or admit it, as in 'I allow that you are right'.

clue.text: American volume a boy produced, one letter at a time

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of litre, a unit of volume
Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad brings out an American book, spelt out painstakingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests a book, but it is a measure of capacity, spelt the American way.
explanation.definitionFit: Literatim is Latin for letter by letter, describing exact transcription.

clue.text: Country in which the author settles again?

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as I
to reland is to come down to earth a second time

explanation.surface: A writer wonders which country to move back to.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'the author' or 'the setter' often stands for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a nation in north-west Europe, an example of a country.

clue.text: Bit of hair included in covering letter

indicators.note: the answer is contained within the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A lock of hair is enclosed with a covering letter, as a keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curly lock, so a small portion of someone's hair.

clue.text: Keel over, so to speak, being half-drunk?

indicators.note: signals that the word for heeling over is to be said out loud

parts.note: a ship that keels over lists, leaning to one side

explanation.surface: A tipsy person is liable to topple over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brahms and Liszt' is British rhyming slang for drunk ('pissed'), so the composer's name is half of that drunk phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang pairs two composers for 'sozzled', and the second name is one half of it.

clue.text: Source of oil that Van Gogh used to paint

definitions.meaning: its seeds are pressed for a cooking oil

definitions.text: that Van Gogh used to paint
definitions.meaning: the Dutch artist painted a famous series of these yellow flowers

explanation.surface: Something the painter relied on for his oil paints.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant yields seed oil and was the subject of a celebrated set of still lifes by the Dutch painter.

clue.text: Polish husband spotted outside

indicators.note: the word for spotted goes outside, around the husband

parts.note: spotted means seen

explanation.surface: A Polish husband was seen out and about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality, but it is the lustre on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish here is a noun meaning a glossy shine, which is what sheen means.

clue.text: Given bad marks outside gym, ran away

indicators.note: the word for given bad marks sits outside, around the gym

parts.note: scarred means left with marks or blemishes
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A pupil marked down outside the gym has fled.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarper is British slang for run away, so scarpered means fled.

clue.text: I approach animal shelter seriously

parts.note: to near is to approach
a nest is a home built by an animal

explanation.surface: Someone earnestly walks up to a creature's den.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sincerely and with serious intent.

clue.text: Be held up in clearing, opting not to pass

indicators.note: the turned word goes in the word for clearing

parts.note: ridding means freeing or clearing of something

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Be delayed in a forest clearing, choosing not to move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reverses the word because this is a down clue. In bridge a player either bids again or says 'pass', so 'opting not to pass' is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games such as bridge, bidding again means making another bid rather than passing.

clue.text: Financial expert giving English firm clear forecast

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a forecast of clear weather would be no mist

explanation.surface: An expert advises an English company on its outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: An economist studies the economy and money, so is an expert on finance.

clue.text: Spears or shoots cat in dramatic situation

definitions.meaning: the edible young stems of a vegetable, sold as spears
in T S Eliot's cat poems, Gus the Theatre Cat has this as his full name

explanation.walkthrough: Gus, the old cat of the playhouse in Eliot's Old Possum poems (and the musical Cats), is short for this.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is eaten as its young shoots, and the theatre cat in Eliot's verse bears its name.

clue.text: Flourish as Joyce's hero

definitions.meaning: Leopold, the central figure of James Joyce's Ulysses

explanation.surface: Joyce's central character thrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloom is to flower and thrive, and it is also the surname of the protagonist of Ulysses.

clue.text: A head arrayed, oddly, in pirate cap

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a strange order, so they are mixed up

explanation.surface: A buccaneer is oddly dressed in a pirate hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Per capita is Latin for 'by heads', meaning for each person.

clue.text: King Albert climbing inside to have a hot bath, say

definitions.text: to have a hot bath, say

indicators.note: the short name goes within the word for king

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards

parts.note: Al is short for Albert

explanation.surface: King Albert climbs into a hot bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses the short name because this is a down clue; 'say' marks a hot bath as just one example of unwinding.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaking in a hot bath is an example of unwinding, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Quick drink about four

indicators.note: the drink goes around the number, about it

parts.note: ale is a drink
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A quick drink for a group of four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' looks like it describes the drink, but it is the old sense meaning living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its old sense means living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.

clue.text: Sleep rough without resistance? Rubbish!

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, the word for sleeping rough surrounds the resistance

parts.note: to doss is to sleep rough or in makeshift lodging
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A complaint that sleeping on the streets without any resistance is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is waste or worthless matter, so rubbish.

clue.text: Place in Texas half-heartedly served up vegetarian dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is read from the bottom upwards
half of the doubled letter at the centre of the word is lost

parts.note: Dallas is a city in Texas

explanation.surface: A Texan city serves up a meat-free plate with little enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two central Ls, leaving DALAS, which 'served up' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad is a dish of raw vegetables, typically one with no meat.

clue.text: Hunt the poet, led by artist, navigator and author

indicators.note: the poet's name comes after, led by, the artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Leigh Hunt was an English Romantic poet, so his first name

explanation.surface: The poet Hunt follows an artist, a seafarer and a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan explorer who also wrote a history of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan explorer and writer of poems and a world history.

clue.text: First to subscribe, minimally

definitions.meaning: to sign with just the first letters of one's name

explanation.definitionFit: The word means first, and as a verb it means marking a document with just the opening letters of your name.

clue.text: South in military vessel

definitions.meaning: the southern states of the USA
an army cooking pot or mess tin

explanation.surface: Down South aboard a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a nickname for the American South and also an army cooking pot or mess tin.

clue.text: Very happy it's not serious, getting caught in the act

indicators.note: the light-hearted word is trapped inside the act, held within it

parts.note: a deed is an act
something light is not serious

explanation.surface: Glad that it was only a minor matter when caught red-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Delighted is a synonym of overjoyed, meaning greatly pleased.
